title: Memory Marker

location.series: COLLINS / Figma / Nothing Great Is Made Alone case study

slide_intent: Repeat a distinctive cue across formats because viewers need something familiar when the content changes.
strategic_value: Colored contributor labels can connect Figma’s print, social and website communications as one collaborative story.
demonstration: Orange circles and arrows connect colored name labels across a Mona Lisa poster, social music illustration and tablet website.
practical_value: Choose a small recurring cue that can survive changes in medium and subject.

content_islands.name: Print example
content_islands.spec: Place the annotated portrait at left with circles around selected contributor labels.

content_islands.name: Social example
content_islands.spec: Place the music post in the middle and point to its label.

content_islands.name: Web example
content_islands.spec: Place the tablet at right and connect its contributor labels back to the other formats.

reference_purposes.Intent: The Memory Marker caption explicitly describes a repeated cue as an aid to recognition and recall.
reference_purposes.Application: Arrows trace contributor labels across print, social and web examples.

ingredient.name: Contributor labels
ingredient.role: Make separate contributors visible and connect campaign formats.
ingredient.application: Pair short names or roles with colored cursor-like tools and carry the pairing across formats.
ingredient.scope: Demonstrated campaign examples; no mandatory label colors, positions or dimensions are specified.
